items.title: Food World Plus opens in Mississauga as Ontario’s largest grocery store
items.summary: Grocery shopping just got a whole lot bigger. Ontario’s largest grocery store has officially opened its doors in Mississauga, bringing flavours, ingredients and cuisines from countries and regions around the world under one roof. Food World Plus opened to shoppers on Oct. 30, welcoming residents from across the GTA to explore its massive 176,000-square-foot facility at 50 Matheson Blvd. East. The grocery store has made global food its main selling point, highlighting products and ingredients from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. With such a wide range of international offerings, the store is looking to cater to Mississauga’s diverse population while giving shoppers access to ingredients they might otherwise have to visit multiple specialty grocery stores to find. Beyond its international food selection, Food World Plus is also positioning itself as a one-stop shopping destination, with a range of departments including a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and in-house butcher. Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo was in attendance for the store’s grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford. Tedjo later took to social media to welcome the new addition to the city. “Food World Plus has everything you need and more! ” Tedjo said in an Instagram post. One of the store’s standout offerings is its dedicated halal section within the meat department. According to Food World Plus, the meat is sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards, from delivery to the cuts prepared for customers.

items.title: A school in Toronto and one in Mississauga dramatically improved EQAO scores. Here’s how they pulled it off
items.summary: Lessons from the TDSB’s Corvette Junior Public School in Scarborough and PDSB’s Brian W. Fleming in Mississauga. Ryan and Jayden work on a math question in Grade 3 at Corvette Junior Public School in Scarborough last month. How far did the protesters march along a pipeline route? That was part of the question facing Grade 5-6 students at Corvette Junior Public School, huddled in small groups, working through a math problem involving distances and subtraction. As their teacher moved through the class offering guidance, Shaun, Fariya and Tanvi joined forces. They wrote equations. Explained their reasoning. And used addition to check their answer. “It’s fun,” says Shaun about math. “Sometimes it can be hard and challenging. ” At this school, there’s time to tackle the challenges. The “balanced day” schedule gives students 100 minutes of uninterrupted math daily — 40 more than the province requires — and 100 for literacy. The extra time in math permits longer lessons, group work and class discussions to identify struggling students.

items.title: This GTA drive-thru Christmas show has tunnels and 2 million twinkling lights
items.summary: Journey into Enchantment runs on select nights from Nov. 20 to Dec. 26. Journey into Enchantment has illuminated tunnels. A drive-thru Christmas light show with more than two million twinkling lights is back in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) for another season, and it’s ready for its set up in Ajax this year. Journey into Enchantment, which has been running in the GTA for six years, combines a drive-thru light show, a walk-thru display and meet-and-greets with Santa Claus and friends, all included in one ticket. The show runs on select nights from Nov. 20 to Dec. 26 at 462 Kingston Rd. E. The 45-minute experience starts with a two-kilometre drive past glowing Christmas scenes and through illuminated tunnels, with lights that move in time to classic holiday songs. The fun doesn’t end when you park. Admission also includes a 15-minute outdoor walk-thru featuring 2D and 3D light displays, including a giant illuminated gingerbread house and towering NOEL letters. items.title: Felician Sisters Weigh Next Step for Shuttered Mississauga Catholic School After Farewell Mass
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto, hundreds of alumnae and staff gathered Saturday for a final mass marking the end of their former Catholic high school. The gathering closed out Holy Name of Mary College School, a Mississauga institution that shut its doors in June. CBC reported the school closed due to low enrolment. The 62 year old building's future remains uncertain, the broadcaster said. Its owners, the Felician Sisters of St. Francis, have not yet decided what will happen to the property, according to CBC.

items.summary: Canada's Bianca Andreescu defeated American Elizabeth Mandlik 6-3, 6-3 to win the Cundinamarca Open title on Saturday in Sopo, Colombia.

items.title: Heavy police presence in Mississauga neighbourhood after fatal early-morning stabbing
items.summary: A man has died after a stabbing inside a home in Mississauga early Saturday morning. m. on Saturday (Nov. 14). Police say an altercation happened inside the home, and a man was stabbed. He died of his injuries. Police say there is currently no evidence to suggest a threat to public safety. There is a large police presence in the area, and residents are asked to avoid it. Police have not released the man’s identity or age, or said whether anyone has been arrested. Police say more information will be released as it becomes available. Anyone with information is asked to contact Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311, referencing incident number PR260386225. Anonymous tips can be made to Peel Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

items.title: Toronto Police Name Two Suspects, Including a Teen, in Fatal Etobicoke Shooting of Mississauga Man
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Toronto police have issued Canada-wide warrants for two suspects in the fatal shooting of an 18-year-old Mississauga man in Etobicoke on Nov. 7. Officers found the victim with gunshot wounds and attempted life-saving measures before paramedics took him to hospital, where he later died, insauga.com reported. The suspects fled before police arrived. In an update issued Saturday, police said they identified Armani Callender, 19, and Cameron Marlor, 17, both of Toronto, as wanted on Canada-wide warrants, according to the outlet. Police said they obtained a judge's permission to publicly name Marlor despite his age, an order that expires at noon on Thursday, Nov. 19, insauga.com reported. Investigators have released images of both suspects. Police have not said which charges relate to which suspect, or whether anyone else was hurt, according to the outlet.

items.title: Mississauga Could Delay Opening Four Outdoor Rinks as El Nino Threatens a Milder Winter
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a forecasted strong El Nino weather pattern could disrupt municipal services this fall and winter, including delays opening outdoor skating rinks. The city said El Nino is a natural global pattern that recurs every two to seven years, marked by warmer than average sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific. The pattern tends to bring milder weather to western and Central Canada, according to the Government of Canada. The city said a longer, milder fall and slower start to winter are expected, which experts say may be intensified by climate change. Mississauga warned that freeze thaw cycles could affect outdoor rinks, trees and infrastructure. Warmer temperatures make it harder to maintain rink ice, the city said. Mississauga said it may delay the planned Nov. 21 opening of its four outdoor rinks due to safety concerns.
